scope: Portability audit of the Strata engine, packer, server, installer, and accelerator seam for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. This is a static source and published-artifact analysis plus arithmetic on published shapes. It does NOT build a backend, convert a checkpoint, download 475 GiB, or run one token of DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, and it does not prove any speed, quality, or fitment claim.

derived_scale_arithmetic.note: Computed from the published shapes above; not a measurement of a converted artifact.

model_geometry.attention_families: GDN linear-attention layers + QSA sparse full-attention layers (every 4th)

compatibility_matrix.component: serve/ (OpenAI+Anthropic API, web app, MCP, monitoring)
compatibility_matrix.why: Model-agnostic protocol surface; only tokenizer/chat-template inputs and the engine subprocess contract are model-specific.

compatibility_matrix.component: setup.py installer and its host detection
compatibility_matrix.verdict: reusable with a new family entry
compatibility_matrix.why: RAM-to-model selection, download, card detection, and launch are architecture-independent; --family/--model would need a deepseek entry and new artifact URLs.
Backend-neutral ABI v1 router_logits_bf16 operation; the Qwen router shape is a parameter, not a hard-coded contract.

compatibility_matrix.component: Expert tiering infrastructure (expert_cache, peer_experts, remote_experts, foresight_swap, dma_batch, expert_source, hit_hook)
compatibility_matrix.why: Slots, residency table, profile ranking, hit/miss split, and DMA staging are geometry-agnostic; every expert-bytes and slot-count constant changes.

compatibility_matrix.component: GGUF split reader and mmap (gguf_split, GgufModel, artifact/dequant)
compatibility_matrix.why: Generic GGUF v3 parsing, shard index, duplicate-tensor refusal, and dequantizers are not architecture-bound; only the arch guard and accepted type list change.

compatibility_matrix.component: Platform and memory tier (direct_file, memory, pinned, vmm)
compatibility_matrix.why: No Qwen literals; general-purpose I/O and pinning.

compatibility_matrix.component: Speculative decoding policy (spec/, draft_policy, suffix_drafter, coupled_draft, verify)
compatibility_matrix.why: Acceptance policy, verify window, and sampler coupling are model-agnostic; only the draft source differs (DeepSeek ships DSpark + 3 MTP layers, not a Qwen MTP).

compatibility_matrix.component: MoE expert math (native_moe, grouped expert kernels, shared_expert, cpu/expert)
compatibility_matrix.verdict: reusable in structure, not in types
compatibility_matrix.why: Grouped top-k expert execution and the shared-expert add are the same operation; gate/up/down byte layouts must be re-implemented for FP4 E2M1 + per-32 UE8M0 scales, which no current kernel decodes.
Strata pins softmax over all experts with top-10 renormalisation; DeepSeek uses sqrtsoftplus scores, a noaux_tc auxiliary-corrected top-6, and routed_scaling_factor 1.5, with a separate vision bias.

compatibility_matrix.component: Dense layers (attention, MLA-style q/o LoRA, hyper-connections)
compatibility_matrix.why: Strata's Qwen block is Qwen-specific: GDN linear attention or QSA, hc=4 with hc_lr=320 and 3 dense mixer matrices per sublayer. DeepSeek has q_lora_rank/o_lora_rank/o_groups and mHC with Sinkhorn mixing over hc_mult=4 copies.

Both select a top-k of cached KV positions with an auxiliary indexer, but DeepSeek CSA2 shares KV and index keys across Full/Reindex/Reuse layers over a 128-token sliding window plus compressed latent KV with per-layer compress_ratios, and adds a hierarchical candidate-block stage. Strata's QSA is per-layer 4-cell-block pooling over its own geometry.
DeepSeek's global KV is FP4 E2M1 with one E4M3 scale per 16 channels and SWA-bounded replay; Strata has INT8/INT4 pools with its own cell layout.

Strata's PLE is a 320M-row 90-byte table read 16 rows per token from SSD; DeepSeek's Engram is 2 tables of ~384M rows x 256 dims with prime-modulus n-gram hashing, a compressed 99,092-token vocab, and 3 lookback sizes x 8 heads per token. The hash, row width, and lookup fan-out all change.

Strata's MtpDrafter is transcribed from llama.cpp's qwen4_exp single MTP layer; DeepSeek ships 3 MTP layers plus a separate DSpark semi-autoregressive block with its own Markov head, confidence head, and 128-expert MoE.

Strata's per-cell (t,h,w) M-RoPE table is generic; the Qwen ViT-style encoder and Strata's image-token PLE hashing are Qwen-specific, and DeepSeek uses a DeepSeek-ViT with 2D-RoPE, 3x3 unshuffle downsampling, and a 2-layer aligner.
The struct's defaults are the Qwen model; every field differs and the per-tensor name/shape assertions are keyed to blk.N.* names.
Build graph, backend flags, and the SYCL migration model do not name a model.

measured_reuse_surface.note: Counts are ripgrep line matches for Qwen-specific literals (2560, 10240, hc_lr, qwen4exp, NG_N_EMBD, n_expert = 512, top-10/topk_512) per directory; they bound coupling, not effort.

blockers_to_running_on_strix.note: Strix has 8 GiB VRAM and 91.4 GiB RAM. V4.1-Flash needs ~475 GiB of weights before any KV cache.
reasons: Published checkpoint is ~475 GiB (510.3 GB) across 48 shards; Strix RAM is ~91 GiB.
Engram tables alone are ~183 GiB at FP8 or ~366 GiB at BF16.
Routed experts alone are ~253 GiB at the shipped FP4.
Community GGUF ports exist (vcruz305, JigSawPT, smalinin) but require a patched llama.cpp; they are not the artifact Strata loads, and Strata's loader requires general.architecture == qwen4exp.

recommendation.verdict: Treat as a second model family, not a port.
recommendation.rationale: The reusable part is the runtime shell (server, installer, tiering design, artifact plumbing, plugin ABI, speculative policy). The part that must be written is the whole model core: geometry, tensor names, router semantics, attention/CSA2, KV quantisation, Engram, MTP/DSpark, and the FP4/FP8 decode paths.
recommendation.cheapest_correct_first_step: Stand up the published PyTorch reference (inference/model.py + convert.py + kernel.py) on the B550 dual-3090Ti host with --expert-dtype fp8 and a small max_seq_len to prove real decode, then decide whether a Strata C++/CUDA implementation is worth it. A B550-only 552B MoE will still be far too small, so treat this as a correctness harness, not a capacity plan.
recommendation.alternative_first_step: Evaluate whether an existing patched llama.cpp (vcruz305/llama.cpp/patches/patch_llamacpp_v41.py) is sufficient before committing to a Strata implementation.

non_claims: No DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash weights were downloaded and no Strata code was built or modified for this audit.
The derived GiB figures are arithmetic on published shapes, not measurements of a converted or requantized artifact.
This audit does not claim the port is impossible; it claims the model-specific core must be written and the target does not fit the Strix box as shipped.
Community GGUF ports were identified by search only; their fidelity, patch completeness, and output agreement with the official implementation were not verified.
No upstream project was contacted or contributed to, per the standing no-upstreaming policy.
